This view tells the 2026 Field Marketing story with one lens. Every lead and contact created in 2026 through a field event, followed stage by stage. The focus is action, especially on the open leads that have not yet moved.

1What you're looking at

The Cohort Summary is anchored on the date a lead or contact was created in 2026. From there, the funnel unfolds across stages: open leads, disqualified leads, MQLs, SQLs, won, lost and revenue. Open Leads is the highlighted bucket because that's where action lives. Everything else is a stage we have already taken a call on.

2How to use the Summary

Start at the top. The Open Leads number tells you how much addressable audience is sitting untouched. Click a month to see which events contributed, then click any number in any row to drill into the actual records behind it. Filters let you slice by region, event or product. Reset clears everything.

Where to spend energy. The Open Leads column is the leverage point. A high Open Lead count next to a low MQL count for the same event means there is unworked pipeline. Coordinate with SDRs.

3The Event × Month grid

Pick any metric from the dropdown and read it across the year by event. This is the single best view to compare how events perform side by side, month by month. Useful when planning the next quarter's calendar.

4The asterisk you'll see

A few events have an asterisk next to their name. These are 2026 list uploads of attendees from older events. They are real 2026 leads, but the event itself was older. Counted in the cohort because the lead is fresh, called out because the event isn't.

One question to bring to every conversation with this view: of the open leads in front of us, which event produced them, and who is following up? The rest is reporting. This is the action.
